# Atomic intrinsics

The atomic loads, stores, exchanges and read-modify-write operations, memory orders and fences that the Atomic package builds on.

<h2 id="memory-order"><code>MemoryOrder</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum MemoryOrder: uint8 {
    Relaxed = 0,
    Acquire = 1,
    Release = 2,
    AcquireRelease = 3,
    SequentiallyConsistent = 4
}
```

Which other memory operations may be reordered across an atomic one.
The weakest ordering that makes a program correct is also the fastest, and a stronger one is never wrong. When in
doubt, `SequentiallyConsistent` gives every thread one agreed order of all such operations.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L15)

**Cases**

| Name                     | Value | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Relaxed`                | `0`   | No ordering: the operation itself is atomic, and nothing around it is held back. Right for counters whose value no other memory depends on.                                                                         |
| `Acquire`                | `1`   | Later operations of this thread are not moved before this load, so whatever a releasing thread wrote before its release is visible after this acquire. For loads and the read half of read-modify-write operations. |
| `Release`                | `2`   | Earlier operations of this thread are not moved after this store, so they are visible to a thread that acquires what it stores. For stores and the write half of read-modify-write operations.                      |
| `AcquireRelease`         | `3`   | Both `Acquire` and `Release`, for a read-modify-write operation that does both.                                                                                                                                     |
| `SequentiallyConsistent` | `4`   | `AcquireRelease`, and also a single order of every sequentially consistent operation that all threads agree on.                                                                                                     |

<h2 id="atomic-load"><code>AtomicLoad&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AtomicLoad<T>(address: *T, order: MemoryOrder) -> T
```

Reads the value at `address` atomically.
`order` must be `Relaxed`, `Acquire` or `SequentiallyConsistent`, written at the call. `address` must be aligned to
the size of `T` and point at memory every thread that touches it reaches only through atomic operations. Runs in
constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L40)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `T`  | an integer of 8 to 64 bits, `bool`, or a pointer |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type          | Description                                     |
| --------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `address` | `*T`          | the value to read                               |
| `order`   | `MemoryOrder` | which other operations may move across this one |

**Returns**: the value read

<h2 id="atomic-store"><code>AtomicStore&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AtomicStore<T>(
    address: *var T,
    value: T,
    order: MemoryOrder

```

Writes `value` to `address` atomically.
`order` must be `Relaxed`, `Release` or `SequentiallyConsistent`, written at the call. `address` must be aligned to
the size of `T`. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L50)

| ---- | ------------------------------------------------ |

| --------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `address` | `*var T`      | where to write                                  |
| `value`   | `T`           | what to write                                   |
| `order`   | `MemoryOrder` | which other operations may move across this one |

<h2 id="atomic-exchange"><code>AtomicExchange&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AtomicExchange<T>(
    address: *var T,
    value: T,
    order: MemoryOrder
) -> T
```

Writes `value` to `address` and returns what was there, as one atomic step.
Any ordering is allowed. `address` must be aligned to the size of `T`. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L60)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `T`  | an integer of 8 to 64 bits, `bool`, or a pointer |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type          | Description                                     |
| --------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `address` | `*var T`      | where to write                                  |
| `value`   | `T`           | what to write                                   |
| `order`   | `MemoryOrder` | which other operations may move across this one |

**Returns**: the value that was replaced

<h2 id="atomic-compare-exchange"><code>AtomicCompareExchange&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AtomicCompareExchange<T>(
    address: *var T,
    expected: T,
    desired: T,
    success: MemoryOrder,
    failure: MemoryOrder
) -> T
```

Writes `desired` to `address` if it holds `expected`, and returns what it held, as one atomic step.
The write happened exactly when the returned value equals `expected`. `success` orders the operation when it writes,
and `failure` when it only reads; `failure` may not be `Release` or `AcquireRelease`, nor acquire more than
`success` does. `address` must be aligned to the size of `T`. Never fails spuriously. Runs in constant time apart
from contention and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L75)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `T`  | an integer of 8 to 64 bits, `bool`, or a pointer |

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type          | Description                                           |
| ---------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `address`  | `*var T`      | the value to compare and replace                      |
| `expected` | `T`           | the value `address` must hold for the write to happen |
| `desired`  | `T`           | the value to write                                    |
| `success`  | `MemoryOrder` | the ordering when the write happens                   |
| `failure`  | `MemoryOrder` | the ordering when it does not                         |

**Returns**: the value `address` held before the operation

<h2 id="atomic-fetch-add"><code>AtomicFetchAdd&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AtomicFetchAdd<T>(
    address: *var T,
    value: T,
    order: MemoryOrder
) -> T
```

Adds `value` to the integer at `address` and returns what was there, as one atomic step.
The sum wraps on overflow, as two's complement arithmetic does. Any ordering is allowed. Runs in constant time apart
from contention and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L87)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description                |
| ---- | -------------------------- |
| `T`  | an integer of 8 to 64 bits |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type          | Description                                     |
| --------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `address` | `*var T`      | the integer to add to                           |
| `value`   | `T`           | what to add                                     |
| `order`   | `MemoryOrder` | which other operations may move across this one |

**Returns**: the value before the addition

pub func AtomicFetchSub<T>(

<h2 id="atomic-fetch-and"><code>AtomicFetchAnd&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AtomicFetchAnd<T>(
    address: *var T,
    value: T,
    order: MemoryOrder

```

Combines the value at `address` with `value` by bitwise and, and returns what was there, as one atomic step.
Any ordering is allowed. Runs in constant time apart from contention and allocates nothing.

<h2 id="fence"><code>Fence</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Fence(order: MemoryOrder)
```

Orders this thread's memory operations without touching memory.
`order` must not be `Relaxed`, which would order nothing. An `Acquire` fence keeps later operations after earlier
loads, a `Release` fence keeps earlier operations before later stores, and `SequentiallyConsistent` does both and
takes part in the single order of sequentially consistent operations. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L137)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type          | Description               |
| ------- | ------------- | ------------------------- |
| `order` | `MemoryOrder` | what the fence holds back |

<h2 id="spin-hint"><code>SpinHint</code></h2>

```rux
pub func SpinHint()
```

Tells the processor that the thread is waiting in a loop for another thread.
It saves power and lets a sibling hardware thread run, and has no effect on memory. A loop that waits long should
sleep instead. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Atomic.rux#L143)
